From the second independent review (2026-11), each case reproduced on 2.0.22 first (tests/test_review_2.py):
What could cut a wrong garment
- A corrected order whose making again failed: the file made before (old measurement) stayed in the nesting queue and
  was cut. A model is nested only while it is the newest thing written for its order line.
- The new one made but the old file not movable to the archive: both were cut.
- A base pattern corrected while orders wait, their XML not readable again: cut from the old pattern. They are made again
  from the order as it was read, and not nested before.
- After one refusal of LEVEL7 Nesting the customer's gaps and the one-marker nesting were dropped for the whole run.
- "Read again" removed the order line before reading the file (replaced, cut short, no customer found: the order gone).
- One XML measurement filling two Xs: both went to the X carrying the XML code (a garment 570 mm long instead of 1570).
- The same order line sent again under the same revision number with corrected data was ignored without a word.
What stopped the line or lost an order
- The program closed between "XML read" and "order made": never made. Made at the next look.
- While the drawing program could not work every order was blocked and its XML moved to error: they wait and are made
  by themselves.
- One customer's cutting folder away stopped every customer's nesting; LEVEL7 Nesting there but not startable failed
  every order of the queue.
- The wait text stayed in the window; a file dated ahead was left out of the queue; the pattern check said "sound"
  for orders it cannot compare with a base pattern.
Licence (as LEVEL7 Nesting 2.0.22): far last day, newest policy for the command line, no policy older than version 4,
no device code without the computer's id, a way out of the clock lock, files written in one step (tried again, then in
place, when another program holds the file open on Windows).
(Build 23 was stopped before it finished: the last point was added after it started.)
